title: Oathbound Formation Core
summary: A four-follower Goodly Folk shell that places two Formation units in front of a verified Archer and Wizard backline.
bestFor: Learning formation spacing, leader-first building, and verified equipment limits.
strengths: Two verified Formation units provide a readable frontline starting point.
Archer and Wizard keep distinct ranged and spell roles behind the line.
Every equipped item fits the public Gear or Trinket capacity shown by its bearer.
weaknesses: The arrangement is an editorial draft and has no published win-rate evidence.
Wizard has low public HP and can reduce STR for adjacent allies.
The complete equipment plan represents shopping goals, not a guaranteed shop sequence.
planningNote: Keep the Wizard separated from STR-dependent allies and revise the line after checking the live board.

title: Ranged Cover Line
summary: A compact week-three company that protects the Archer with two verified Formation units and avoids unsupported equipment assumptions.
bestFor: Players who want a small, readable ranged formation before expanding the company.
strengths: Only three follower cells are occupied, so the plan is quick to understand and revise.
The Archer's verified Backline tactic and Longshot skill support a protected ranged role.
Feather Charm matches the Archer's public AGI requirement and Trinket capacity.
weaknesses: The Archer's public card has low HP and no armor.
A small line can lose coverage when an enemy reaches the backline.
The two-handed Bow of Grace is deliberately excluded because the public Archer card lists only one Gear slot.
planningNote: Use this as an early board shell; expand only after confirming the next active cells and the live shop.

title: Ivo Arcane Reserve
summary: An Ivo-led planning shell that uses the Wizard's verified INT, MP, Gear, and Trinket capacity without treating the loadout as permanent best-in-slot.
bestFor: Reviewing a spell-focused shopping plan alongside a durable verified screen.
strengths: Ivo's public leader trait discounts Trinkets by 1G.
Wizard exceeds the published requirements for Wand, Frostfall, and Ruby Charm.
Goodly Knight and Portly Knight provide verified Formation bodies in front.
weaknesses: Wizard's public 10 HP makes poor positioning costly.
Quick-Witted reduces STR for adjacent allies, so tight grouping can hurt the screen.
The listed item cost is a planning total, not proof that all items appear in one run.
planningNote: Preserve space around the Wizard and treat the three-item loadout as a purchase priority list.

title: Bone Host Flank Pair
summary: A compact Young Keth company using the two complete Bone Host cards currently available in the verified archive.
bestFor: Exploring verified Flanking, Respawn, and ally-death interactions without inventing missing roster data.
strengths: Skeleton Child and Skeleton Dog both have verified public Flanking tactics.
Respawn and Feast create two different ways to react when the board changes.
The small week-two layout is easy to move and compare.
weaknesses: Only two complete Bone Host unit cards are currently available in the source layer.
No equipment is preloaded because complete public slot capacity is not available for both units.
Flanking does not guarantee a useful target or safe return position.
planningNote: Treat this as a verified mechanic sketch, then add name-only roster units manually only when you accept the missing public card data.

title: Mixed Verified Field Test
summary: A Multiplayer-only test board containing all six complete public unit cards so players can compare roles in one editable company.
bestFor: Comparing every verified unit card and then pruning the board into a focused multiplayer plan.
strengths: Uses all six complete public unit cards currently available in the archive.
Combines Formation, Backline, and Flanking tactics on one board.
The Builder can immediately move, remove, or re-equip every placed record.
weaknesses: Mixed factions are allowed here only because the preset uses Multiplayer rules.
The board is a comparison workspace, not a tested recommendation or ranked composition.
Different movement and adjacency behaviors can pull the formation apart.
planningNote: Remove the roles that do not support your intended plan; do not treat six verified records as proof of one coherent meta team.
